A-19 | When water intake is "too low" (FR-6 verification) | Any time today's total is below the student's water goal, the daily summary includes a "water intake is low" message. Reaching the goal shows a "goal reached" message instead. | FR-6 RTM verification method (D1 §4.4)
A-20 | Point values and limits | UREC visit: 10 points, awarded only for the first visit of each day (later swipes are still recorded). Reaching the daily step goal: 5 points, once per day. A-21 | What the leaderboard ranks and who appears on it | Rank = point balance (ties share a rank), among the student and their friends. A-22 | What `isPublic` controls | Non-friends viewing a private profile see only the username, not the display name or member-since date. Search by username always works, so friend requests are still possible. | D1 §5.2 User.isPublic; FR-3; Prop §4 "user-entered public information"

An alert fires when a service goes down (first down check) and again when it recovers, not on every check. | D1 UC-4 "Raise Downtime Alert"; SD-4 alt [service down]
A-25 | Which "servers" are monitored, how often, how long records are kept | 7 components named after the §5.3.2 boxes (api-gateway, auth-gateway, nutrition-service, activity-service, social-service, admin-service, database), each with a real probe. A-29 | Editing or deleting logged meals, water or visits | Not provided; the spec only describes logging and viewing. | D1 UC-1, UC-2

A-31 | Brute-force protection and rate limiting | Not implemented (out of scope for the course prototype). The login error message is the same for every failure, so usernames can't be probed. | D1 NFR Security

A-33 | (stage 2) How to keep a no-Docker option and fast tests after the switch to MySQL; what happens to stage-1 PostgreSQL data | The `h2` profile and the test profile use H2 in MySQL mode with the same Flyway SQL. The V1 migration was rewritten in MySQL syntax (foreign keys as table constraints, `DATETIME(6)` timestamps) because a new database product starts empty; stage-1 PostgreSQL/H2 data is not migrated (it was test data only). | TRC README; D1 §5.3.2 "Encrypted Database"
A-34 | (stage 2) How the team's WATER_LOG table and LogWater unit fit the app's schema: column names, user id type, and what "fullName" is (team USERS has firstName/lastName; the class diagram User has only displayName) | Table `water_log(id, user_id BIGINT -> users.id, amount FLOAT(24) liters, logged_at DEFAULT now)`: the team's columns in this schema's snake_case and with the users key type (the team's `userId VARCHAR(64)` cannot reference an INT/BIGINT key). A-35 | (stage 2) Water inputs that LogWater does not cover: missing amount, an amount that truncates to 0.00 L, very large amounts, ml input, floating-point truncation error | Missing -> 400 "Amount is required." A-38 | (stage 2) D2 §2.4.1 lists FR-1..FR-7 only, while D2 §2.4.3 (UC-1 "2,6,8") and §2.4.4 RTM still list FR-8 (UTD Dining nutritional information) | Treated as a copy omission in the draft, not a removal: FR-8 and its features stay. | D2 §2.4.1, §2.4.3, §2.4.4; D1 §4.1
A-39 | (stage 2) TD-1 details: how the authenticator app is opened, what "larger screen" means, how a device is remembered | "Add to authenticator app" opens the standard `otpauth://totp/CometFit:<username>?secret=…&issuer=CometFit` link (account filled in); if nothing opens, the app says to use "Copy setup key". The setup key stays visible as selectable text. QR shown when the window is at least 768 px/dp wide. "Remember this device for 30 days" is a checkbox next to the code field. When checked and the code is valid, the server issues a random 256-bit device token, stores only its SHA-256 hash with a 30-day expiry, and the client keeps the token per username (browser localStorage, phone secure store). A remembered sign-in still needs the password, does not extend the 30 days, and only works for the same user. Changing the password forgets all remembered devices. A login with neither code nor device token is rejected as a malformed request (400) before the password is checked; every credential failure still gets one generic 401 message (A-31). | TD-1; D1 NFR Security; A-3, A-6, A-31 **SUPERSEDED in part by `spec/03-team-decisions/TD-5.md`: (a) the code field and the "Remember this device for 30 days" checkbox are no longer on the sign-in screen; sign-in asks username + password only, and the code + checkbox are on a second "Verify it's you" screen shown only when the device is not remembered (TD-5 (1), (2)); (b) the 400 "neither code nor device token" rule is gone: the password step without a remembered device returns 200 with a single-use challenge and no session (TD-5 (2)), see A-42; (c) "QR shown when the window is at least 768 px/dp wide" is replaced by "QR on every screen size" at the setup step (TD-5 (3)). A-40 | (stage 2) TD-2 details: what "some activity history" is, and how UC-3 can show more than one person on the leaderboard | On a fresh database, alice and bob are seeded as friends (the leaderboard and friend stats only cover friends, A-21) with 7 days (6 past days + today up to the current time) of fixed demo data: 3 manual meals/day (labelled "(demo)"), 500 ml water refills, steps from a linked simulated watch (DEMO-WATCH-ALICE / -BOB), some UREC visits at UREC-FRONT-1, and the matching points (A-20: 10 per first daily visit, 5 for reaching 10 000 steps). A-41 | (stage 2) Proposal feature not carried into D1/D2 requirements: "a map showing the different and closest areas to refill their water" | **Intentionally excluded** (decided by the team in `spec/03-team-decisions/TD-3.md`): out of scope for this version; no map, location or refill-station feature is built. FR-6 water logging is unaffected. | Prop §3 Project Objectives; D1/D2 FR-1..FR-8, UC-1..UC-4; TD-3
A-42 | (stage 3) TD-5 "short-lived, single-use challenge": how long it lives, how many wrong codes it allows, how it is sent | `POST /api/auth/login` {username, password, deviceToken?} returns either a session (remembered device) or `verificationRequired: true` + a random 256-bit `challengeId` and no token. `POST /api/auth/verify` {challengeId, totpCode, rememberDevice} completes it. Sign-in challenge lives 5 minutes; the setup challenge after Register 15 minutes (time to install Duo Mobile and scan). Deleted on success (single-use) and after 5 wrong codes; a wrong code before that keeps it so the user can retype. Only its SHA-256 hash is stored (table `login_challenges`); expired rows are purged hourly with sessions. Every failure (unknown/expired/used challenge, wrong code, wrong password) is the same generic 401 (A-31). | TD-5 (2), (5); D1 §5.2 AuthService; NFR Security
A-43 | (stage 3) TD-5 (3) registration: does the account exist before the first code is entered; what if the user leaves the setup screen | The account is created when Register is pressed (A-3, unchanged); Register returns the setup key / otpauth link and a setup challenge but no session. Entering the first valid code on "Set up two-step verification" completes the challenge and signs the user in (the "Remember this device" checkbox is offered there too). 7. Built foundation: V1 schema (one table per §5.2 class), User/Student/Developer/Session, AuthService (password BCrypt + TOTP RFC 6238), AES-GCM field encryption, BaseController, API gateway interceptor (feature-flag routing), Auth/Profile controllers, demo seeder. Commit "Foundation".

1	// UC-1 "View Daily Summary & Goals" — SD-1 "updated daily summary -> display calories, macros, water progress".
2	// FR-2 (calories), FR-6 (water, low-intake message), steps from FR-4 sync. NFR Safety warnings are listed too.
3	import React from 'react';
4	import { RefreshControl, ScrollView, Text } from 'react-native';
5	import { api } from '../api';
6	import { progress } from '../logic';
7	import { Banner, Card, colors, MaintenanceNotice, ProgressBar, Row, s, Stat } from '../ui';
8	import { useAsync } from '../useAsync';
9	
10	export default function TodayScreen({ refreshKey }: { refreshKey: number }) {
11	  const { data, error, loading, reload } = useAsync(() => api.summary(), [refreshKey]);
12	
13	  if (error?.isMaintenance) return <MaintenanceNotice name="Nutrition & Hydration" />;
14	
15	  return (
16	    <ScrollView refreshControl={<RefreshControl refreshing={loading} onRefresh={reload} />}>
17	      {error ? <Banner kind="error">{error.message}</Banner> : null}
18	      {data ? (
19	        <>
20	          <Text style={[s.h1, { marginBottom: 10 }]}>Today ({data.date})</Text>
21	          {data.messages.map((m) => (
22	            <Banner key={m} kind={m.startsWith('Water goal reached') ? 'good' : 'warn'}>{m}</Banner>
23	          ))}
24	          <Card title="Calories">
25	            <Text style={s.body}>
26	              {data.calories} / {data.calorieGoal} kcal
27	            </Text>
28	            <ProgressBar value={progress(data.calories, data.calorieGoal)} color={data.calories > data.calorieGoal ? colors.warn : colors.primary} />
29	            <Row>
30	              <Stat label="Protein" value={`${data.proteinG} g`} />
31	              <Stat label="Carbs" value={`${data.carbsG} g`} />
32	              <Stat label="Fat" value={`${data.fatG} g`} />
33	              <Stat label="Meals" value={String(data.mealCount)} />
34	            </Row>
35	          </Card>
36	          <Card title="Water">
37	            <Text style={s.body}>
38	              {data.waterLiters.toFixed(2)} L ({data.waterMl} / {data.waterGoalMl} ml)
39	            </Text>
40	            <ProgressBar value={progress(data.waterMl, data.waterGoalMl)} color="#2A8BD8" />
41	            <Text style={s.muted}>
42	              That's {(data.waterMl / data.bottleSizeMl).toFixed(1)} bottles of {data.bottleSizeMl} ml.
43	            </Text>
44	          </Card>
45	          <Card title="Steps">
46	            <Text style={s.body}>
47	              {data.steps} / {data.stepGoal} steps
48	            </Text>
49	            <ProgressBar value={progress(data.steps, data.stepGoal)} color={colors.good} />
50	            <Text style={s.muted}>
51	              {data.latestHeartRate ? `Latest heart rate: ${data.latestHeartRate} bpm` : 'Connect a smart device in Activity to sync steps.'}
52	            </Text>
53	          </Card>
54	        </>
55	      ) : null}
56	    </ScrollView>
57	  );
58	}

# Build log

1. Read `PROMPT.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, listed `spec/01-canvas-submitted/` (2 PDFs).
2. Extracted text of `Team_9_SE3354_F26_ProjectProposal.pdf` and `Team_09_SE3354_F26_Deliverable_1.pdf` with `pdftotext -layout` (printed to stdout, nothing written into `spec/`).
3. Tried to render diagram pages: `pdftoppm` not installed and Read-tool PDF rendering also needs poppler -> failed. Fix: wrote scratch tool `app/.spec-render/extract-images.js` (Node, zlib only) that pulls embedded image XObjects out of the PDF and re-encodes them as PNG. 10 images extracted (git-ignored).
4. Viewed all 10 images: Fig 4.3 use case diagrams UC-1..UC-4, SD-1..SD-4 sequence diagrams (§5.1), class diagram (§5.2), client-server architecture diagram (§5.3.2).
5. Checked environment: Java 23.0.1, Maven 3.9.11, Node 22.23, npm 10.9. Docker CLI present but Docker Engine not running -> PostgreSQL via docker-compose is provided for the README, and an embedded H2 profile is used to build/test/run here (see A-2).
6. Backend stack chosen (general programming, not product): Spring Boot 3.4 (Java 21 target on JDK 23), JPA + Flyway, PostgreSQL / H2. `mvn dependency:resolve` OK.
7. Built foundation: V1 schema (one table per §5.2 class), User/Student/Developer/Session, AuthService (password BCrypt + TOTP RFC 6238), AES-GCM field encryption, BaseController, API gateway interceptor (feature-flag routing), Auth/Profile controllers, demo seeder. Commit "Foundation".
8. Smoke boot via `mvn spring-boot:run` in background: could not inspect (background output dir and `curl` denied by permissions). Fix: wrote `ContextLoadsTest` (H2) instead -> passes, proving Flyway schema == JPA mappings.
9. UC-1 backend: NutritionController, DailySummaryService, DiningMenuService, AIFoodService + FakeAIFoodService stub, UtdDiningFeed + StubUtdDiningFeed. Commit.
10. UC-2 backend: ActivityController, PointsService, SmartDeviceGateway + FakeSmartDeviceGateway stub, FakeUrecCardReader stub, IntegrationKeyVerifier. Commit.
11. UC-3 backend: SocialController, PrivacyService (filterByConsent), leaderboard. Commit.
12. UC-4 backend: AdminController, MonitoringService, HealthProbes, FeatureFlag endpoints for the app, MonitoringAgentStub, LoggingAlertNotifier stub, OutageSimulator stub, docker-compose + Dockerfile. ContextLoadsTest still green. Commit.
13. Client scaffold: `npx create-expo-app app/client --template blank-typescript` (Expo SDK 58, RN 0.88), then `npx expo install react-dom react-native-web @expo/metro-runtime expo-image-picker`. Read the image-picker API from its installed `.d.ts` files (no web docs).
14. Problem: the template added `app/client/AGENTS.md` (tells agents to fetch Expo docs from the web, against CLAUDE.md rule 8) and `app/client/.claude/settings.json` (enables an Expo plugin). `rm` and writes into `.claude/` need approval I could not get. Fix: replaced AGENTS.md with a short note, did not follow its instructions, and git-ignored both files. The template's untracked `LICENSE` was left uncommitted.
15. Wrote client: `api.ts`, `types.ts`, `logic.ts`, `ui.tsx`, `smartDevice.ts` (FakeSmartDevice stub), screens Login, Today, Log, Activity, Friends, Profile, AdminDashboard; `App.tsx` (student tabs + module guard, developer dashboard). `tsc --noEmit` clean; `npx expo export --platform web` bundles (468 KB). Committed per use case (UC-1..UC-4 client commits).
16. Server tests: ApiTestSupport + SecurityTest, TotpTest (RFC 6238 vectors), Uc1..Uc4 tests, MonitoringServiceTest. First run: 36/38. 2 failures came from the test helper double-encoding `%20` in MockMvc URLs; fixed the test, now 38/38 pass.
17. Client tests (`node --test --experimental-strip-types`): first failed because `node --test <dir>` is not supported on Node 22 -> used a glob; then failed on a TS constructor parameter property (unsupported by type stripping) -> rewrote it as an explicit field. 7/7 pass. Excluded `__tests__` from the app `tsc` run.
18. Wrote `app/tools/totp.mjs` and `app/tools/smoke.mjs` (end-to-end HTTP walk of UC-1..UC-4 with the demo accounts). First run hit a stale server on :8099 (TaskStop on the earlier `mvn spring-boot:run` left its forked JVM alive, still serving foundation-era code) -> ran the fresh build on :8098: 23/23 smoke checks pass; CORS preflight from http://localhost:8081 OK. Two orphaned smoke-test JVMs (ports 8098, 8099, in-memory DBs) could not be killed without approval; reported to the user.
19. Not verified here: the PostgreSQL profile (Docker Engine not running; same Flyway SQL, validated on H2 in PostgreSQL mode), and visual rendering of the client in a real browser (no browser automation available). Only the web bundle build and typecheck were verified for the client.
20. Wrote `app/README.md`, `ASSUMPTIONS.md` (A-1..A-32), `TRACEABILITY.md` (FR-1..FR-8, UC-1..UC-4 + sub-use-cases, NFRs, class/sequence/architecture artefacts -> code and tests). Commit.

## Stage 2 (2026-11-14): update to Deliverable 2 draft, team repo code, team decisions

Instruction: `proof/prompts/stage-2.md` (same text as the stage-2 prompt). Precedence when documents disagree
(later wins): Proposal, Deliverable 1, Deliverable 2 draft, team repo code (for the unit it covers), team decisions.

21. Re-read `PROMPT.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and every file in `spec/`: Proposal + D1 (`pdftotext -layout`, stdout only),
    `spec/02-deliverable-2-draft/` (README + PDF), `spec/03-team-decisions/` (README, TD-1..TD-3),
    `spec/04-team-repo-code/` (README, README-SOURCE, LogWater.java, LogWaterTest.java, run.sh, db/docker-compose.yml, db/init.sql).
22. Extracted the D2 PDF images with `app/.spec-render/extract-images.js` into `app/.spec-render/img-d2/` (git-ignored).
    Pixel-compared them with the D1 images: the 7 carried-forward diagrams (sequence diagrams SD-1..SD-4, class diagram
    §2.5.2, architecture §2.5.3, Fig 4.3) are **byte-identical** to D1. 3 new images = D2 §4.2 screenshots of
    `LogWater.java`, `LogWaterTest.java` and the JUnit output "OK (3 tests)"; they match the files in `spec/04-team-repo-code/`.
    D1's three use-case-diagram images are not in the D2 draft (§2.4.3 keeps only the table). Treated as a draft omission, not a change.
23. Baseline before any change: `mvn test` all green (38 tests).

### Stage 2 steps

24. D-1 MySQL: replaced the PostgreSQL driver/Flyway module with `mysql-connector-j` + `flyway-mysql`; rewrote V1 in MySQL syntax (MySQL ignores inline `REFERENCES`, so foreign keys became table constraints; `DATETIME(6)`); H2 test/no-Docker profile switched to MySQL mode; docker-compose now `mysql:8.4` and the server starts with plain `docker compose up` (D-13). `mvn test` 38/38 on H2.
25. Stopped the stage-1 containers and deleted the old `app_cometfit-db` PostgreSQL volume (stage-1 smoke-test leftovers). First `docker compose up --build` failed inside Docker BuildKit ("parent snapshot ... does not exist", an engine cache error, not the build); the retry built fine. Flyway applied V1 on MySQL 8.4, Hibernate schema validation passed, `node app/tools/smoke.mjs`: 23/23 pass on MySQL.
26. D-2..D-7 water unit: V2 migration creates `water_log` (liters, FLOAT(24)), copies old entries (ml -> liters, truncated) and drops `water_entries`. `WaterLogService.enter(userId, amount, isLiter)` mirrors team `LogWater.enter` (same messages, gallon factor, truncation). `POST /api/nutrition/water` takes `amount` + `isLiter` (and still `volumeMl`) and returns `message`; the summary adds `waterLiters`. Found while writing it: `Math.floor(0.29 * 100)` = 28 in IEEE doubles (the team code has the same issue); fixed with a 1e-9 guard (A-35). Tests: new `WaterLogTest` (TC-1..TC-3 port + 4 more) and 2 API tests in `Uc1NutritionTest` (D2 §4.1 three 500 mL refills = 1,500 mL; negative/missing messages). Every pre-existing test passes unchanged: 47/47. Client: L/gal input, server message shown, liters on Today/Log; 2 new client tests (9/9), `tsc` clean. Smoke test +2 checks. On MySQL in Docker, V2 applied and the earlier 500 ml entry became 0.5 L; 25/25 smoke checks pass.
27. D-8/D-9 TD-1: server V3 `trusted_devices` (hash only), `AuthService.login(..., rememberDevice, deviceToken)`, password change forgets devices. First test run: 1 failure in the existing `SecurityTest` (it expects 400, not 401, when the code is missing). Fixed by keeping that contract: a login with neither code nor device token is a 400 checked before credentials, so it reveals nothing about the password. New `RememberDeviceTest` (6), 53/53 server tests. Client: `npx expo install expo-clipboard expo-secure-store`, `npm install qrcode @types/qrcode` (npm registry only; no docs read). LoginScreen: "Add to authenticator app" (otpauth link), "Copy setup key", QR drawn with Views when width >= 768, "Remember this device for 30 days" checkbox, password-only sign-in on a remembered device. 3 new client tests (12/12), `tsc` clean, web export OK (512 KB). On MySQL in Docker V3 applied; smoke +2 TD-1 checks, all pass. Not verified: the QR scan with a real phone and `Linking.openURL(otpauth://…)` opening a real authenticator app (no phone here).
28. D-10 TD-2: `DemoDataSeeder` now turns on all sharing for alice and bob, makes them friends, and writes 7 days of fixed history (meals, water, steps via a linked simulated watch, UREC visits, points), only when both are newly created. New `DemoDataTest` (2 tests: real numbers + 2-person leaderboard; new accounts still share nothing). 55/55 server tests. `docker compose down -v` + `up --build`: seed log "alice and bob are friends, share all stats, 7 days of history"; smoke shows leaderboard "1.alice:65 2.bob:30"; all checks pass.
29. D-11 TD-3: confirmed no map/refill-location code exists; recorded as intentionally excluded (A-41) and in TRACEABILITY "Excluded on purpose". D-12: FR-8 kept (A-38).
30. TRACEABILITY rewritten: new "Sources" table (Prop, D1, D2 §2 and §4, TRC, TD-1..TD-3), FR-6 / UC-1 / UC-3 / Log In rows updated, new TD-1 rows, "Test documentation (D2 §4)" table mapping TC-1..TC-3 to `WaterLogTest`, D1 §x = D2 §2.x section mapping, database now MySQL. `app/README.md`: `docker compose up --build` runs everything, clean-reset steps (`down -v`), new env vars (`DB_ROOT_PASSWORD`, `COMETFIT_REMEMBER_DEVICE_DAYS`), TD-1 sign-in, TD-2 demo data, liters/gallons, test counts, changed request bodies, demo script. A-1..A-32 reviewed: A-2, A-3, A-6, A-18 are answered by the new inputs and marked SUPERSEDED (rows kept); the others still apply (A-32: D2 mentions Figma prototype screens, but they are not in `spec/`).
31. Final verification: `mvn test` 55/55 (38 stage-1 tests unchanged + 17 new); client `npm test` 12/12, `tsc` clean, web export OK. Docker: `docker compose down -v` then plain `docker compose up -d` (MySQL 8.4 + server); 3 migrations applied, TD-2 seed logged; `smoke.mjs` 25/25 (the 2 friend-request checks are skipped because the demo students are already friends). Then `down -v` + `up -d` once more so the demo starts from clean seeded data (no smoke-test leftovers); stack left running. Not verified here: client rendering in a real browser or phone, the QR scan, and `otpauth://` opening an authenticator app. The stage-1 H2 file `app/server/data/cometfit*` (PostgreSQL mode, git-ignored) is no longer used (new file name `cometfit-mysql`) and was left in place.

## Stage 3 (TD-4 prototype look, TD-5 two-step sign-in)

32. Read the stage-3 instruction, TD-4, TD-5 and viewed every PNG in `spec/05-ui-prototype/` (1-sign-in, 2-dashboard, 3-food-water, 4-social, 5-activities, 6-account, all-screens). Reviewed the two commits left by the stopped first stage-3 run: `9bf70c1` (shared theme, headers with initials avatar, 5-tab bar) is kept; `897c1dc` (sign-in styled like the prototype but with the code field on the sign-in screen) is kept for its styling and the sign-in flow is redone for TD-5 in step (c).
33. (a) TD-5 server: V4 `login_challenges` (hash only), `LoginChallenge` entity + repository; `AuthService.authenticate(username, password, deviceToken)` now returns a session only for a remembered device, otherwise a single-use challenge; new `verifyChallenge(challengeId, code, rememberDevice)` (5 min, 5 wrong codes, `noRollbackFor` so the attempt counter survives the 401); `startSetup` after Register. `POST /api/auth/login` lost `totpCode`/`rememberDevice`; new `POST /api/auth/verify`; `/register` returns `setupChallengeId`. Tests changed because TD-5 changes their behavior: `ApiTestSupport.login` uses the two steps; `SecurityTest.loginRequiresPasswordAndValidTotp` (old 400 for a missing code is gone, A-39 superseded); `RememberDeviceTest` (checkbox moved to /verify; a foreign/expired device token now leads to step 2 instead of 401). New `TwoStepSignInTest` (8) covers TD-5 (5). `mvn test` 63/63 first try. `tools/smoke.mjs` uses the two steps. `docker compose up -d --build server`: V4 applied on MySQL; smoke 28/28 (alice, bob, dev sign in; remembered device skips step 2). The smoke run adds a few entries to the demo data (as in stage 2).
34. (b) Theme + tab bar: kept `9bf70c1` as is (palette, `ScreenHeader` with initials avatar, `Segmented`, `ListRow`, `RankRow`, `LetterBadge`, five tabs with the prototype titles/subtitles). Found that its comments cite A-42/A-43 and `897c1dc` cites A-44, but the stopped run never wrote those rows, and A-42/A-43 are now the TD-5 rows. Fixed: comments renumbered to A-44 (hex values) and A-45 (Dashboard not guarded as a whole), rows added.
35. (c) TD-5 client: new `src/authFlow.ts` (pure: `submitPassword` sends username + password + stored device token, returns signed-in or a challenge, forgets a device the server no longer accepts; `submitCode` completes the challenge and saves the device token; `toSession` never treats a challenge as a session). `api.login` no longer takes a code; new `api.verify`; `LoginStep` / `Registration.setupChallengeId` types. `LoginScreen` rewritten as four steps: Sign in (username + password only), Register (details only), Verify it's you (large 6-digit field, "Remember this device for 30 days" checkbox, Back to sign in), Set up two-step verification (QR on every screen size sized by `qrCellSize`, "Add to authenticator app", "Copy setup key", first code + checkbox, Finish setup signs in). Kept from `897c1dc`: wordmark + centered title layout and no Microsoft button (A-46).

# Assumptions

Every gap that had to be filled because `spec/` (Project Proposal = "Prop", Deliverable 1 = "D1", Deliverable 2 draft = "D2",
team repo code = "TRC", team decisions = "TD-n") is silent or ambiguous. Code comments reference these IDs.
Rows answered by a later input are kept and marked **SUPERSEDED by ...** (stage 2).

A-n | what was missing | choice made | related spec section
---|---|---|---
A-1 | How the "Server" box (API gateway, auth gateway, 4 services, encrypted DB) is deployed; load balancing / telemetry details | One Spring Boot process with one package per box: `gateway` (API gateway + module routing), `security` (auth gateway), `controllers`+`services` (Social / Activity / Nutrition / Admin), PostgreSQL. Load balancing is not built for a laptop demo; telemetry = health checks + uptime records (FR-1). | D1 §5.3.1, §5.3.2, §5.3.3
A-2 | Which database product; Docker Engine not running on the build machine | PostgreSQL 16 (docker-compose) is the default. An `h2` Spring profile (embedded file DB, PostgreSQL mode) lets the app run and be tested without Docker. The same Flyway schema is used for both. | D1 §5.3.2 "Encrypted Database"; Prop §9 "Database for the app" **SUPERSEDED by `spec/04-team-repo-code/README.md` ("MySQL for database operations") and `db/docker-compose.yml` (`mysql:8.4`): database is now MySQL 8.4; see A-33.**
A-3 | How accounts are created (every use case includes "Log In" but there is no sign-up use case) | Students self-register (username, password, email, display name) and get a TOTP secret to add to an authenticator app. Developer accounts are created by seed/config only. | D1 Fig 4.3 "Log In (Password + TOTP)"; NFR Security **SUPERSEDED (TOTP setup part) by `spec/03-team-decisions/TD-1.md` (1), (2): after sign-up the app shows "Add to authenticator app" and "Copy setup key", and a QR code only on larger screens; self-registration itself is unchanged. See A-39.**
A-4 | Credential rules | Username 3–30 chars `[A-Za-z0-9_.]`, unique (case-insensitive); password ≥ 8 chars; email must look like an address. | NFR Security
A-5 | What "all user data will be encrypted" means concretely | Passwords: BCrypt hash. Email and TOTP secret: AES-256-GCM field encryption (key from `COMETFIT_DATA_KEY`). Other tables (meals, steps, …) rely on database/disk-level encryption in a real deployment, because the app must sum and query them. TLS is expected from the deployment's reverse proxy; the local demo uses plain HTTP. | NFR Security, NFR Legislative-Security; D1 §5.3.2 "Encrypted Database"
A-6 | Login flow detail and session lifetime | One login call carries username + password + 6-digit TOTP code; a Session (random 256-bit token, Bearer header) is created only if both factors pass, and lasts 12 h. `AuthService.authenticate` therefore takes the TOTP code as a third argument. TOTP = RFC 6238, SHA-1, 30 s, ±1 step. | D1 §5.2 AuthService, Session; NFR Security **SUPERSEDED (code on every sign-in) by `spec/03-team-decisions/TD-1.md` (3): "Remember this device for 30 days"; a remembered device signs in with username + password only. Session lifetime and TOTP parameters unchanged. See A-39.**
A-7 | Default goals for a new student | 2000 kcal, 2000 ml water, 10 000 steps, 500 ml bottle. Students can change them. | D1 §5.2 Student (calorieGoal, waterGoalMl, stepGoal)
A-8 | Where the water-bottle size lives (Prop: "volume of the user's water bottle … number of refills"; SD-1 "log water (bottle size / refill)"; class diagram has no field) | Added `bottleSizeMl` to Student (set in Profile → Goals). The app logs a refill as `saveWaterEntry(bottleSizeMl)`, plus half bottle or a custom amount. | Prop §4; D1 SD-1
A-9 | What "daily" means (time zone of the day boundary) | Configurable `COMETFIT_ZONE`, default America/Chicago (D1 cites the Texas Data Privacy and Security Act, so the users are in Texas). | D1 UC-1 "View Daily Summary & Goals"
A-10 | Thresholds for an "unsafe goal" | Warn when calorie goal < 1200 or > 4000 kcal, water goal < 1000 or > 4000 ml, step goal > 30 000 (Prop risk "User over-exertion → Warnings of the app"). The goal is still saved; the app only warns (NFR says "allow a warning"). | D1 NFR Safety; Prop §8
A-11 | Which "portions of the app" can be shut down | Three modules, each mapped to an API prefix: NUTRITION (`/api/nutrition`), ACTIVITY (`/api/activity`), SOCIAL (`/api/social`). Login, profile and admin cannot be disabled. A disabled module answers 503 `MODULE_DISABLED`, and the client shows a maintenance notice on those tabs. | FR-5; D1 UC-4, SD-4 ("disable module (e.g. Friends)")
A-12 | How external systems (UREC card reader, monitoring service) authenticate | Shared secret in header `X-Integration-Key` (`COMETFIT_INTEGRATION_KEY`). Card readers must also be registered in `urec_card_readers`; seed reader `UREC-FRONT-1` at "UREC front desk". | D1 §5.3.2 External Systems; SD-2, SD-4; NFR Security
A-13 | Names and contents of the "backend permissions list" | Students implicitly hold `nutrition.use`, `activity.use`, `social.use`, `profile.use`. Developers hold an explicit list; the seeded developer has `admin.uptime.view`, `admin.modules.manage`, `profile.use`. Developers do not get student features. | D1 NFR Security; §5.2 Developer.permissions; UC-4 "Authorize Admin (Permissions + TOTP)"
A-14 | Data for a recorded demo | When `COMETFIT_SEED_DEMO=true` (default), seed developer `dev` and students `alice` and `bob`, password `CometFit123!`, with fixed, published TOTP secrets. Demo only; turn it off anywhere real. | PROMPT (demoable in a video)

The estimate is shown for review and is saved only after the student confirms or edits it. The photo itself is not stored. | D1 UC-1 "Log Meal by Photo"; SD-1; Prop §2
A-16 | UTD Dining menu content and locations | Stub feed with two locations, "Dining Hall" and "Campus Store" (from FR-8's rationale "campus stores and dining hall"), and 5 placeholder items each. A-19 | When water intake is "too low" (FR-6 verification) | Any time today's total is below the student's water goal, the daily summary includes a "water intake is low" message. Reaching the goal shows a "goal reached" message instead. | FR-6 RTM verification method (D1 §4.4)
A-20 | Point values and limits | UREC visit: 10 points, awarded only for the first visit of each day (later swipes are still recorded). Reaching the daily step goal: 5 points, once per day. Points are never deducted. | Prop §3 "point based system"; D1 UC-2 "Earn Points", SD-2 `awardPoints(studentId, VISIT)`
A-21 | What the leaderboard ranks and who appears on it | Rank = point balance (ties share a rank), among the student and their friends. A-23 | How the friend is "notified of request" (Prop excludes push notifications) | In-app only: the request appears in the receiver's *Friend requests* list. | D1 SD-3 "notify of request"; Prop §4 Out of Scope

A-25 | Which "servers" are monitored, how often, how long records are kept | 7 components named after the §5.3.2 boxes (api-gateway, auth-gateway, nutrition-service, activity-service, social-service, admin-service, database), each with a real probe. # Assumptions

Every gap that had to be filled because `spec/` (Project Proposal = "Prop", Deliverable 1 = "D1", Deliverable 2 draft = "D2",
team repo code = "TRC", team decisions = "TD-n") is silent or ambiguous. Code comments reference these IDs.
Rows answered by a later input are kept and marked **SUPERSEDED by ...** (stage 2).

A-n | what was missing | choice made | related spec section
---|---|---|---
A-1 | How the "Server" box (API gateway, auth gateway, 4 services, encrypted DB) is deployed; load balancing / telemetry details | One Spring Boot process with one package per box: `gateway` (API gateway + module routing), `security` (auth gateway), `controllers`+`services` (Social / Activity / Nutrition / Admin), PostgreSQL. Load balancing is not built for a laptop demo; telemetry = health checks + uptime records (FR-1). | D1 §5.3.1, §5.3.2, §5.3.3
A-2 | Which database product; Docker Engine not running on the build machine | PostgreSQL 16 (docker-compose) is the default. An `h2` Spring profile (embedded file DB, PostgreSQL mode) lets the app run and be tested without Docker. The same Flyway schema is used for both. | D1 §5.3.2 "Encrypted Database"; Prop §9 "Database for the app" **SUPERSEDED by `spec/04-team-repo-code/README.md` ("MySQL for database operations") and `db/docker-compose.yml` (`mysql:8.4`): database is now MySQL 8.4; see A-33.**
A-3 | How accounts are created (every use case includes "Log In" but there is no sign-up use case) | Students self-register (username, password, email, display name) and get a TOTP secret to add to an authenticator app. Developer accounts are created by seed/config only. | D1 Fig 4.3 "Log In (Password + TOTP)"; NFR Security **SUPERSEDED (TOTP setup part) by `spec/03-team-decisions/TD-1.md` (1), (2): after sign-up the app shows "Add to authenticator app" and "Copy setup key", and a QR code only on larger screens; self-registration itself is unchanged. See A-39.**
A-4 | Credential rules | Username 3–30 chars `[A-Za-z0-9_.]`, unique (case-insensitive); password ≥ 8 chars; email must look like an address. | NFR Security
A-5 | What "all user data will be encrypted" means concretely | Passwords: BCrypt hash. Email and TOTP secret: AES-256-GCM field encryption (key from `COMETFIT_DATA_KEY`). Other tables (meals, steps, …) rely on database/disk-level encryption in a real deployment, because the app must sum and query them. TLS is expected from the deployment's reverse proxy; the local demo uses plain HTTP. | NFR Security, NFR Legislative-Security; D1 §5.3.2 "Encrypted Database"
A-6 | Login flow detail and session lifetime | One login call carries username + password + 6-digit TOTP code; a Session (random 256-bit token, Bearer header) is created only if both factors pass, and lasts 12 h. `AuthService.authenticate` therefore takes the TOTP code as a third argument. TOTP = RFC 6238, SHA-1, 30 s, ±1 step. | D1 §5.2 AuthService, Session; NFR Security **SUPERSEDED (code on every sign-in) by `spec/03-team-decisions/TD-1.md` (3): "Remember this device for 30 days"; a remembered device signs in with username + password only. Session lifetime and TOTP parameters unchanged. See A-39.**
A-7 | Default goals for a new student | 2000 kcal, 2000 ml water, 10 000 steps, 500 ml bottle. Students can change them. | D1 §5.2 Student (calorieGoal, waterGoalMl, stepGoal)
A-8 | Where the water-bottle size lives (Prop: "volume of the user's water bottle … number of refills"; SD-1 "log water (bottle size / refill)"; class diagram has no field) | Added `bottleSizeMl` to Student (set in Profile → Goals). The app logs a refill as `saveWaterEntry(bottleSizeMl)`, plus half bottle or a custom amount. | Prop §4; D1 SD-1
A-9 | What "daily" means (time zone of the day boundary) | Configurable `COMETFIT_ZONE`, default America/Chicago (D1 cites the Texas Data Privacy and Security Act, so the users are in Texas). | D1 UC-1 "View Daily Summary & Goals"
A-10 | Thresholds for an "unsafe goal" | Warn when calorie goal < 1200 or > 4000 kcal, water goal < 1000 or > 4000 ml, step goal > 30 000 (Prop risk "User over-exertion → Warnings of the app"). The goal is still saved; the app only warns (NFR says "allow a warning"). | D1 NFR Safety; Prop §8
A-11 | Which "portions of the app" can be shut down | Three modules, each mapped to an API prefix: NUTRITION (`/api/nutrition`), ACTIVITY (`/api/activity`), SOCIAL (`/api/social`). Login, profile and admin cannot be disabled. A disabled module answers 503 `MODULE_DISABLED`, and the client shows a maintenance notice on those tabs. | FR-5; D1 UC-4, SD-4 ("disable module (e.g. Friends)")
A-12 | How external systems (UREC card reader, monitoring service) authenticate | Shared secret in header `X-Integration-Key` (`COMETFIT_INTEGRATION_KEY`). Card readers must also be registered in `urec_card_readers`; seed reader `UREC-FRONT-1` at "UREC front desk". | D1 §5.3.2 External Systems; SD-2, SD-4; NFR Security
A-13 | Names and contents of the "backend permissions list" | Students implicitly hold `nutrition.use`, `activity.use`, `social.use`, `profile.use`. Developers hold an explicit list; the seeded developer has `admin.uptime.view`, `admin.modules.manage`, `profile.use`. Developers do not get student features. | D1 NFR Security; §5.2 Developer.permissions; UC-4 "Authorize Admin (Permissions + TOTP)"
A-14 | Data for a recorded demo | When `COMETFIT_SEED_DEMO=true` (default), seed developer `dev` and students `alice` and `bob`, password `CometFit123!`, with fixed, published TOTP secrets. Demo only; turn it off anywhere real. | PROMPT (demoable in a video)
A-15 | Behaviour of the "AI Food Recognition Service" | Stub: picks 1–2 entries from a fixed placeholder table, deterministically from the image's SHA-256. The estimate is shown for review and is saved only after the student confirms or edits it. The photo itself is not stored. | D1 UC-1 "Log Meal by Photo"; SD-1; Prop §2
A-16 | UTD Dining menu content and locations | Stub feed with two locations, "Dining Hall" and "Campus Store" (from FR-8's rationale "campus stores and dining hall"), and 5 placeholder items each. Each `getMenu` call refreshes items from the feed into `dining_items` (keyed by the feed's item id), so meal entries can reference them. | FR-8; D1 UC-1 "Maintain Dining Menu & Macros"; §5.2 DiningItem
A-17 | Meaning of `steps` in a pushed ActivityRecord | Steps counted since the previous sync (an increment). Daily steps = sum of the day's records. Limits per push: steps 0–100 000, heart rate 20–250 bpm. | D1 SD-2 "pushSteps(steps, heartRate, timestamp)"; §5.2 ActivityRecord
A-18 | Default data-sharing consent | All four `share*` flags default to false; nothing is visible to friends until the student turns it on. | D1 NFR Legislative-Privacy; §5.2 ConsentSettings **SUPERSEDED for the seeded demo accounts only by `spec/03-team-decisions/TD-2.md`: alice and bob start with all four sharing flags on. Real new accounts keep everything off (this row still applies to them). See A-40.**
A-19 | When water intake is "too low" (FR-6 verification) | Any time today's total is below the student's water goal, the daily summary includes a "water intake is low" message. Reaching the goal shows a "goal reached" message instead. | FR-6 RTM verification method (D1 §4.4)
A-20 | Point values and limits | UREC visit: 10 points, awarded only for the first visit of each day (later swipes are still recorded). Reaching the daily step goal: 5 points, once per day. Points are never deducted. | Prop §3 "point based system"; D1 UC-2 "Earn Points", SD-2 `awardPoints(studentId, VISIT)`
A-21 | What the leaderboard ranks and who appears on it | Rank = point balance (ties share a rank), among the student and their friends. Points come only from visits and steps, so a friend appears (and their points show in their stats) only if they share visits or steps. | D1 UC-3 "View Leaderboard"; NFR Legislative-Privacy; Prop §7 leaderboard
A-22 | What `isPublic` controls | Non-friends viewing a private profile see only the username, not the display name or member-since date. Search by username always works, so friend requests are still possible. | D1 §5.2 User.isPublic; FR-3; Prop §4 "user-entered public information"
A-23 | How the friend is "notified of request" (Prop excludes push notifications) | In-app only: the request appears in the receiver's *Friend requests* list. | D1 SD-3 "notify of request"; Prop §4 Out of Scope
A-24 | Delivery channel for downtime alerts and when to send one | Stub `LoggingAlertNotifier`: logs a WARN line and keeps the last 50 alerts for the admin dashboard. An alert fires when a service goes down (first down check) and again when it recovers, not on every check. | D1 UC-4 "Raise Downtime Alert"; SD-4 alt [service down]
A-25 | Which "servers" are monitored, how often, how long records are kept | 7 components named after the §5.3.2 boxes (api-gateway, auth-gateway, nutrition-service, activity-service, social-service, admin-service, database), each with a real probe. Checks run every 30 s (configurable); uptime % is the share of successful checks over the chosen window (default 24 h). Records are kept 30 days. | FR-1; D1 SD-4 loop [every interval]; §5.2 MonitoringService.checkIntervalSec
A-26 | Client technology, given "mobile app only, no web application" (Prop §4, §7) vs. the requirement that the demo runs in a browser | Cross-platform Expo / React Native app (NFR Development: "native or cross-platform mobile app"). The same app is run through react-native-web for the laptop demo; this is a way to run the mobile client, not a separate web product. The phone-sized layout is kept. | Prop §4 Out of Scope; D1 NFR Operational, NFR Development; PROMPT
A-27 | What the UREC card carries to identify the student | The card reader sends the student's CometFit user id as `studentId` (the class diagram has no separate card-number field). | D1 SD-2 `recordVisit(studentId, time)`; §5.2 UrecCardReader.sendSwipe(studentId)
A-28 | Smart-device link rules | A health-data permission must be granted before linking (UC-2 «include» Grant Health Permissions). A device can be LINKED to only one student at a time. Unlinking keeps history. In the browser, the OS permission prompt and the wearable are simulated (client `FakeSmartDevice`). Optional automatic sync runs every 60 s while the Activity screen is open. | D1 UC-2, SD-2; NFR Interoperability
A-29 | Editing or deleting logged meals, water or visits | Not provided; the spec only describes logging and viewing. | D1 UC-1, UC-2
A-30 | Range of friend statistics | A friend's stats show today's calories, water and steps (with goals), UREC visits in the last 7 days, point balance, and leaderboard rank, each only if consented. | D1 UC-3 "View Friend's Statistics"; SD-3
A-31 | Brute-force protection and rate limiting | Not implemented (out of scope for the course prototype). The login error message is the same for every failure, so usernames can't be probed. | D1 NFR Security
A-32 | Visual design (Figma designs are not in `spec/`) | Simple neutral card-based layout with a bottom tab bar (Today, Log, Activity, Friends, Profile) and a separate admin dashboard for developers. | D1 NFR Development ("Figma for design"); NFR Usability **SUPERSEDED by `spec/03-team-decisions/TD-4.md` and the prototype screens in `spec/05-ui-prototype/`: prototype colors/cards/headers, five tabs Dashboard, Food & Water, Activities, Social, Account; developer dashboard keeps its own screen in the same style.**
A-33 | (stage 2) How to keep a no-Docker option and fast tests after the switch to MySQL; what happens to stage-1 PostgreSQL data | The `h2` profile and the test profile use H2 in MySQL mode with the same Flyway SQL. The V1 migration was rewritten in MySQL syntax (foreign keys as table constraints, `DATETIME(6)` timestamps) because a new database product starts empty; stage-1 PostgreSQL/H2 data is not migrated (it was test data only). | TRC README; D1 §5.3.2 "Encrypted Database"
A-34 | (stage 2) How the team's WATER_LOG table and LogWater unit fit the app's schema: column names, user id type, and what "fullName" is (team USERS has firstName/lastName; the class diagram User has only displayName) | Table `water_log(id, user_id BIGINT -> users.id, amount FLOAT(24) liters, logged_at DEFAULT now)`: the team's columns in this schema's snake_case and with the users key type (the team's `userId VARCHAR(64)` cannot reference an INT/BIGINT key). The class-diagram attribute `volumeMl` is derived from the liters. The "Added …L to <full name>" message uses the user's display name. Users keep `displayName` (class diagram), so no first/last name fields are added. | TRC `LogWater.java`, `db/init.sql`; D1 §5.2 = D2 §2.5.2 User, WaterEntry
A-35 | (stage 2) Water inputs that LogWater does not cover: missing amount, an amount that truncates to 0.00 L, very large amounts, ml input, floating-point truncation error | Missing -> 400 "Amount is required." (D2 §4.1). `amount <= 0` -> "Negative amount." (TRC). Truncates to 0.00 L -> rejected ("too small"). More than 5 L per entry (the stage-1 limit of 5000 ml) -> rejected ("too large"). `volumeMl` (class diagram `saveWaterEntry(volumeMl)`) is still accepted and converted to liters, so a 355 ml refill is stored as 0.35 L. Truncation adds a 1e-9 guard so exact inputs like 0.29 L are not stored as 0.28 L (binary floating point). Errors are HTTP 400/404 with the team's exact messages, not `java.lang.Error`. | TRC `LogWater.java`; D2 §4.1, §4.3; D1 §5.2 NutritionController
A-36 | (stage 2) Units of water goals and totals once entries are in liters | Goals stay in ml (`Student.waterGoalMl`, class diagram). The daily summary gives both `waterLiters` (sum of stored liters) and `waterMl` (the same total in ml) and compares ml with the goal. Screens show "x.xx L (ml / goal ml)". Input on the Log screen: liters or gallons (L / gal toggle); refill buttons send the bottle size in liters. | D1 §5.2 Student; TRC `LogWater.java`; A-8, A-19
A-37 | (stage 2) Test tool: the team uses JUnit 4.13.2 against MySQL (`run.sh`) | The app keeps JUnit 5 (Spring Boot test starter, same JUnit tool family). # Assumptions

Every gap that had to be filled because `spec/` (Project Proposal = "Prop", Deliverable 1 = "D1", Deliverable 2 draft = "D2",
team repo code = "TRC", team decisions = "TD-n") is silent or ambiguous. Code comments reference these IDs.
Rows answered by a later input are kept and marked **SUPERSEDED by ...** (stage 2).

A-n | what was missing | choice made | related spec section
---|---|---|---
A-1 | How the "Server" box (API gateway, auth gateway, 4 services, encrypted DB) is deployed; load balancing / telemetry details | One Spring Boot process with one package per box: `gateway` (API gateway + module routing), `security` (auth gateway), `controllers`+`services` (Social / Activity / Nutrition / Admin), PostgreSQL. Load balancing is not built for a laptop demo; telemetry = health checks + uptime records (FR-1). | D1 §5.3.1, §5.3.2, §5.3.3
A-2 | Which database product; Docker Engine not running on the build machine | PostgreSQL 16 (docker-compose) is the default. An `h2` Spring profile (embedded file DB, PostgreSQL mode) lets the app run and be tested without Docker. The same Flyway schema is used for both. | D1 §5.3.2 "Encrypted Database"; Prop §9 "Database for the app" **SUPERSEDED by `spec/04-team-repo-code/README.md` ("MySQL for database operations") and `db/docker-compose.yml` (`mysql:8.4`): database is now MySQL 8.4; see A-33.**
A-3 | How accounts are created (every use case includes "Log In" but there is no sign-up use case) | Students self-register (username, password, email, display name) and get a TOTP secret to add to an authenticator app. Developer accounts are created by seed/config only. | D1 Fig 4.3 "Log In (Password + TOTP)"; NFR Security **SUPERSEDED (TOTP setup part) by `spec/03-team-decisions/TD-1.md` (1), (2): after sign-up the app shows "Add to authenticator app" and "Copy setup key", and a QR code only on larger screens; self-registration itself is unchanged. See A-39.**

A-6 | Login flow detail and session lifetime | One login call carries username + password + 6-digit TOTP code; a Session (random 256-bit token, Bearer header) is created only if both factors pass, and lasts 12 h. `AuthService.authenticate` therefore takes the TOTP code as a third argument. TOTP = RFC 6238, SHA-1, 30 s, ±1 step. | D1 §5.2 AuthService, Session; NFR Security **SUPERSEDED (code on every sign-in) by `spec/03-team-decisions/TD-1.md` (3): "Remember this device for 30 days"; a remembered device signs in with username + password only. A-7 | Default goals for a new student | 2000 kcal, 2000 ml water, 10 000 steps, 500 ml bottle. Students can change them. | D1 §5.2 Student (calorieGoal, waterGoalMl, stepGoal)

The app logs a refill as `saveWaterEntry(bottleSizeMl)`, plus half bottle or a custom amount. | Prop §4; D1 SD-1
A-9 | What "daily" means (time zone of the day boundary) | Configurable `COMETFIT_ZONE`, default America/Chicago (D1 cites the Texas Data Privacy and Security Act, so the users are in Texas). | D1 UC-1 "View Daily Summary & Goals"
A-10 | Thresholds for an "unsafe goal" | Warn when calorie goal < 1200 or > 4000 kcal, water goal < 1000 or > 4000 ml, step goal > 30 000 (Prop risk "User over-exertion → Warnings of the app"). The goal is still saved; the app only warns (NFR says "allow a warning"). | D1 NFR Safety; Prop §8
A-11 | Which "portions of the app" can be shut down | Three modules, each mapped to an API prefix: NUTRITION (`/api/nutrition`), ACTIVITY (`/api/activity`), SOCIAL (`/api/social`). Login, profile and admin cannot be disabled. A disabled module answers 503 `MODULE_DISABLED`, and the client shows a maintenance notice on those tabs. | FR-5; D1 UC-4, SD-4 ("disable module (e.g. Friends)")
A-12 | How external systems (UREC card reader, monitoring service) authenticate | Shared secret in header `X-Integration-Key` (`COMETFIT_INTEGRATION_KEY`). Card readers must also be registered in `urec_card_readers`; seed reader `UREC-FRONT-1` at "UREC front desk". | D1 §5.3.2 External Systems; SD-2, SD-4; NFR Security
A-13 | Names and contents of the "backend permissions list" | Students implicitly hold `nutrition.use`, `activity.use`, `social.use`, `profile.use`. Developers hold an explicit list; the seeded developer has `admin.uptime.view`, `admin.modules.manage`, `profile.use`. Developers do not get student features. | D1 NFR Security; §5.2 Developer.permissions; UC-4 "Authorize Admin (Permissions + TOTP)"
A-14 | Data for a recorded demo | When `COMETFIT_SEED_DEMO=true` (default), seed developer `dev` and students `alice` and `bob`, password `CometFit123!`, with fixed, published TOTP secrets. Demo only; turn it off anywhere real. | PROMPT (demoable in a video)
A-15 | Behaviour of the "AI Food Recognition Service" | Stub: picks 1–2 entries from a fixed placeholder table, deterministically from the image's SHA-256. The estimate is shown for review and is saved only after the student confirms or edits it. The photo itself is not stored. | D1 UC-1 "Log Meal by Photo"; SD-1; Prop §2
A-16 | UTD Dining menu content and locations | Stub feed with two locations, "Dining Hall" and "Campus Store" (from FR-8's rationale "campus stores and dining hall"), and 5 placeholder items each. Each `getMenu` call refreshes items from the feed into `dining_items` (keyed by the feed's item id), so meal entries can reference them. | FR-8; D1 UC-1 "Maintain Dining Menu & Macros"; §5.2 DiningItem
A-17 | Meaning of `steps` in a pushed ActivityRecord | Steps counted since the previous sync (an increment). Daily steps = sum of the day's records. Limits per push: steps 0–100 000, heart rate 20–250 bpm. | D1 SD-2 "pushSteps(steps, heartRate, timestamp)"; §5.2 ActivityRecord
A-18 | Default data-sharing consent | All four `share*` flags default to false; nothing is visible to friends until the student turns it on. | D1 NFR Legislative-Privacy; §5.2 ConsentSettings **SUPERSEDED for the seeded demo accounts only by `spec/03-team-decisions/TD-2.md`: alice and bob start with all four sharing flags on. A-19 | When water intake is "too low" (FR-6 verification) | Any time today's total is below the student's water goal, the daily summary includes a "water intake is low" message. Reaching the goal shows a "goal reached" message instead. | FR-6 RTM verification method (D1 §4.4)
A-20 | Point values and limits | UREC visit: 10 points, awarded only for the first visit of each day (later swipes are still recorded). Reaching the daily step goal: 5 points, once per day. A-21 | What the leaderboard ranks and who appears on it | Rank = point balance (ties share a rank), among the student and their friends. A-22 | What `isPublic` controls | Non-friends viewing a private profile see only the username, not the display name or member-since date. Search by username always works, so friend requests are still possible. | D1 §5.2 User.isPublic; FR-3; Prop §4 "user-entered public information"
A-23 | How the friend is "notified of request" (Prop excludes push notifications) | In-app only: the request appears in the receiver's *Friend requests* list. | D1 SD-3 "notify of request"; Prop §4 Out of Scope

A-25 | Which "servers" are monitored, how often, how long records are kept | 7 components named after the §5.3.2 boxes (api-gateway, auth-gateway, nutrition-service, activity-service, social-service, admin-service, database), each with a real probe. A-26 | Client technology, given "mobile app only, no web application" (Prop §4, §7) vs. the requirement that the demo runs in a browser | Cross-platform Expo / React Native app (NFR Development: "native or cross-platform mobile app"). The phone-sized layout is kept. | Prop §4 Out of Scope; D1 NFR Operational, NFR Development; PROMPT

A-28 | Smart-device link rules | A health-data permission must be granted before linking (UC-2 «include» Grant Health Permissions). A device can be LINKED to only one student at a time. A-29 | Editing or deleting logged meals, water or visits | Not provided; the spec only describes logging and viewing. | D1 UC-1, UC-2
A-30 | Range of friend statistics | A friend's stats show today's calories, water and steps (with goals), UREC visits in the last 7 days, point balance, and leaderboard rank, each only if consented. | D1 UC-3 "View Friend's Statistics"; SD-3
A-31 | Brute-force protection and rate limiting | Not implemented (out of scope for the course prototype). The login error message is the same for every failure, so usernames can't be probed. | D1 NFR Security
A-32 | Visual design (Figma designs are not in `spec/`) | Simple neutral card-based layout with a bottom tab bar (Today, Log, Activity, Friends, Profile) and a separate admin dashboard for developers. | D1 NFR Development ("Figma for design"); NFR Usability **SUPERSEDED by `spec/03-team-decisions/TD-4.md` and the prototype screens in `spec/05-ui-prototype/`: prototype colors/cards/headers, five tabs Dashboard, Food & Water, Activities, Social, Account; developer dashboard keeps its own screen in the same style.**
A-33 | (stage 2) How to keep a no-Docker option and fast tests after the switch to MySQL; what happens to stage-1 PostgreSQL data | The `h2` profile and the test profile use H2 in MySQL mode with the same Flyway SQL. A-34 | (stage 2) How the team's WATER_LOG table and LogWater unit fit the app's schema: column names, user id type, and what "fullName" is (team USERS has firstName/lastName; the class diagram User has only displayName) | Table `water_log(id, user_id BIGINT -> users.id, amount FLOAT(24) liters, logged_at DEFAULT now)`: the team's columns in this schema's snake_case and with the users key type (the team's `userId VARCHAR(64)` cannot reference an INT/BIGINT key). A-35 | (stage 2) Water inputs that LogWater does not cover: missing amount, an amount that truncates to 0.00 L, very large amounts, ml input, floating-point truncation error | Missing -> 400 "Amount is required." # Assumptions

Every gap that had to be filled because `spec/` (Project Proposal = "Prop", Deliverable 1 = "D1", Deliverable 2 draft = "D2",
team repo code = "TRC", team decisions = "TD-n") is silent or ambiguous. Code comments reference these IDs.
Rows answered by a later input are kept and marked **SUPERSEDED by ...** (stage 2).

A-n | what was missing | choice made | related spec section
---|---|---|---
A-1 | How the "Server" box (API gateway, auth gateway, 4 services, encrypted DB) is deployed; load balancing / telemetry details | One Spring Boot process with one package per box: `gateway` (API gateway + module routing), `security` (auth gateway), `controllers`+`services` (Social / Activity / Nutrition / Admin), PostgreSQL. Load balancing is not built for a laptop demo; telemetry = health checks + uptime records (FR-1). | D1 §5.3.1, §5.3.2, §5.3.3
A-2 | Which database product; Docker Engine not running on the build machine | PostgreSQL 16 (docker-compose) is the default. An `h2` Spring profile (embedded file DB, PostgreSQL mode) lets the app run and be tested without Docker. The same Flyway schema is used for both. | D1 §5.3.2 "Encrypted Database"; Prop §9 "Database for the app" **SUPERSEDED by `spec/04-team-repo-code/README.md` ("MySQL for database operations") and `db/docker-compose.yml` (`mysql:8.4`): database is now MySQL 8.4; see A-33.**
A-3 | How accounts are created (every use case includes "Log In" but there is no sign-up use case) | Students self-register (username, password, email, display name) and get a TOTP secret to add to an authenticator app. Developer accounts are created by seed/config only. | D1 Fig 4.3 "Log In (Password + TOTP)"; NFR Security **SUPERSEDED (TOTP setup part) by `spec/03-team-decisions/TD-1.md` (1), (2): after sign-up the app shows "Add to authenticator app" and "Copy setup key", and a QR code only on larger screens; self-registration itself is unchanged. See A-39.**
A-4 | Credential rules | Username 3–30 chars `[A-Za-z0-9_.]`, unique (case-insensitive); password ≥ 8 chars; email must look like an address. | NFR Security
A-5 | What "all user data will be encrypted" means concretely | Passwords: BCrypt hash. Email and TOTP secret: AES-256-GCM field encryption (key from `COMETFIT_DATA_KEY`). Other tables (meals, steps, …) rely on database/disk-level encryption in a real deployment, because the app must sum and query them. TLS is expected from the deployment's reverse proxy; the local demo uses plain HTTP. | NFR Security, NFR Legislative-Security; D1 §5.3.2 "Encrypted Database"
A-6 | Login flow detail and session lifetime | One login call carries username + password + 6-digit TOTP code; a Session (random 256-bit token, Bearer header) is created only if both factors pass, and lasts 12 h. `AuthService.authenticate` therefore takes the TOTP code as a third argument. TOTP = RFC 6238, SHA-1, 30 s, ±1 step. | D1 §5.2 AuthService, Session; NFR Security **SUPERSEDED (code on every sign-in) by `spec/03-team-decisions/TD-1.md` (3): "Remember this device for 30 days"; a remembered device signs in with username + password only. Session lifetime and TOTP parameters unchanged. See A-39.**
A-7 | Default goals for a new student | 2000 kcal, 2000 ml water, 10 000 steps, 500 ml bottle. Students can change them. | D1 §5.2 Student (calorieGoal, waterGoalMl, stepGoal)
A-8 | Where the water-bottle size lives (Prop: "volume of the user's water bottle … number of refills"; SD-1 "log water (bottle size / refill)"; class diagram has no field) | Added `bottleSizeMl` to Student (set in Profile → Goals). The app logs a refill as `saveWaterEntry(bottleSizeMl)`, plus half bottle or a custom amount. | Prop §4; D1 SD-1
A-9 | What "daily" means (time zone of the day boundary) | Configurable `COMETFIT_ZONE`, default America/Chicago (D1 cites the Texas Data Privacy and Security Act, so the users are in Texas). | D1 UC-1 "View Daily Summary & Goals"
A-10 | Thresholds for an "unsafe goal" | Warn when calorie goal < 1200 or > 4000 kcal, water goal < 1000 or > 4000 ml, step goal > 30 000 (Prop risk "User over-exertion → Warnings of the app"). The goal is still saved; the app only warns (NFR says "allow a warning"). | D1 NFR Safety; Prop §8
A-11 | Which "portions of the app" can be shut down | Three modules, each mapped to an API prefix: NUTRITION (`/api/nutrition`), ACTIVITY (`/api/activity`), SOCIAL (`/api/social`). Login, profile and admin cannot be disabled. A disabled module answers 503 `MODULE_DISABLED`, and the client shows a maintenance notice on those tabs. | FR-5; D1 UC-4, SD-4 ("disable module (e.g. Friends)")
A-12 | How external systems (UREC card reader, monitoring service) authenticate | Shared secret in header `X-Integration-Key` (`COMETFIT_INTEGRATION_KEY`). Card readers must also be registered in `urec_card_readers`; seed reader `UREC-FRONT-1` at "UREC front desk". | D1 §5.3.2 External Systems; SD-2, SD-4; NFR Security
A-13 | Names and contents of the "backend permissions list" | Students implicitly hold `nutrition.use`, `activity.use`, `social.use`, `profile.use`. Developers hold an explicit list; the seeded developer has `admin.uptime.view`, `admin.modules.manage`, `profile.use`. Developers do not get student features. | D1 NFR Security; §5.2 Developer.permissions; UC-4 "Authorize Admin (Permissions + TOTP)"
A-14 | Data for a recorded demo | When `COMETFIT_SEED_DEMO=true` (default), seed developer `dev` and students `alice` and `bob`, password `CometFit123!`, with fixed, published TOTP secrets. Demo only; turn it off anywhere real. | PROMPT (demoable in a video)
A-15 | Behaviour of the "AI Food Recognition Service" | Stub: picks 1–2 entries from a fixed placeholder table, deterministically from the image's SHA-256. The estimate is shown for review and is saved only after the student confirms or edits it. The photo itself is not stored. | D1 UC-1 "Log Meal by Photo"; SD-1; Prop §2
A-16 | UTD Dining menu content and locations | Stub feed with two locations, "Dining Hall" and "Campus Store" (from FR-8's rationale "campus stores and dining hall"), and 5 placeholder items each. Each `getMenu` call refreshes items from the feed into `dining_items` (keyed by the feed's item id), so meal entries can reference them. | FR-8; D1 UC-1 "Maintain Dining Menu & Macros"; §5.2 DiningItem
A-17 | Meaning of `steps` in a pushed ActivityRecord | Steps counted since the previous sync (an increment). Daily steps = sum of the day's records. Limits per push: steps 0–100 000, heart rate 20–250 bpm. | D1 SD-2 "pushSteps(steps, heartRate, timestamp)"; §5.2 ActivityRecord
A-18 | Default data-sharing consent | All four `share*` flags default to false; nothing is visible to friends until the student turns it on. | D1 NFR Legislative-Privacy; §5.2 ConsentSettings **SUPERSEDED for the seeded demo accounts only by `spec/03-team-decisions/TD-2.md`: alice and bob start with all four sharing flags on. Real new accounts keep everything off (this row still applies to them). See A-40.**
A-19 | When water intake is "too low" (FR-6 verification) | Any time today's total is below the student's water goal, the daily summary includes a "water intake is low" message. Reaching the goal shows a "goal reached" message instead. | FR-6 RTM verification method (D1 §4.4)
A-20 | Point values and limits | UREC visit: 10 points, awarded only for the first visit of each day (later swipes are still recorded). Reaching the daily step goal: 5 points, once per day. Points are never deducted. | Prop §3 "point based system"; D1 UC-2 "Earn Points", SD-2 `awardPoints(studentId, VISIT)`
A-21 | What the leaderboard ranks and who appears on it | Rank = point balance (ties share a rank), among the student and their friends. Points come only from visits and steps, so a friend appears (and their points show in their stats) only if they share visits or steps. | D1 UC-3 "View Leaderboard"; NFR Legislative-Privacy; Prop §7 leaderboard
A-22 | What `isPublic` controls | Non-friends viewing a private profile see only the username, not the display name or member-since date. Search by username always works, so friend requests are still possible. | D1 §5.2 User.isPublic; FR-3; Prop §4 "user-entered public information"
A-23 | How the friend is "notified of request" (Prop excludes push notifications) | In-app only: the request appears in the receiver's *Friend requests* list. | D1 SD-3 "notify of request"; Prop §4 Out of Scope
A-24 | Delivery channel for downtime alerts and when to send one | Stub `LoggingAlertNotifier`: logs a WARN line and keeps the last 50 alerts for the admin dashboard. An alert fires when a service goes down (first down check) and again when it recovers, not on every check. | D1 UC-4 "Raise Downtime Alert"; SD-4 alt [service down]
A-25 | Which "servers" are monitored, how often, how long records are kept | 7 components named after the §5.3.2 boxes (api-gateway, auth-gateway, nutrition-service, activity-service, social-service, admin-service, database), each with a real probe. Checks run every 30 s (configurable); uptime % is the share of successful checks over the chosen window (default 24 h). Records are kept 30 days. | FR-1; D1 SD-4 loop [every interval]; §5.2 MonitoringService.checkIntervalSec
A-26 | Client technology, given "mobile app only, no web application" (Prop §4, §7) vs. the requirement that the demo runs in a browser | Cross-platform Expo / React Native app (NFR Development: "native or cross-platform mobile app"). The same app is run through react-native-web for the laptop demo; this is a way to run the mobile client, not a separate web product. The phone-sized layout is kept. | Prop §4 Out of Scope; D1 NFR Operational, NFR Development; PROMPT
A-27 | What the UREC card carries to identify the student | The card reader sends the student's CometFit user id as `studentId` (the class diagram has no separate card-number field). | D1 SD-2 `recordVisit(studentId, time)`; §5.2 UrecCardReader.sendSwipe(studentId)
A-28 | Smart-device link rules | A health-data permission must be granted before linking (UC-2 «include» Grant Health Permissions). A device can be LINKED to only one student at a time. Unlinking keeps history. In the browser, the OS permission prompt and the wearable are simulated (client `FakeSmartDevice`). Optional automatic sync runs every 60 s while the Activity screen is open. | D1 UC-2, SD-2; NFR Interoperability
A-29 | Editing or deleting logged meals, water or visits | Not provided; the spec only describes logging and viewing. | D1 UC-1, UC-2
A-30 | Range of friend statistics | A friend's stats show today's calories, water and steps (with goals), UREC visits in the last 7 days, point balance, and leaderboard rank, each only if consented. | D1 UC-3 "View Friend's Statistics"; SD-3
A-31 | Brute-force protection and rate limiting | Not implemented (out of scope for the course prototype). The login error message is the same for every failure, so usernames can't be probed. | D1 NFR Security
A-32 | Visual design (Figma designs are not in `spec/`) | Simple neutral card-based layout with a bottom tab bar (Today, Log, Activity, Friends, Profile) and a separate admin dashboard for developers. | D1 NFR Development ("Figma for design"); NFR Usability **SUPERSEDED by `spec/03-team-decisions/TD-4.md` and the prototype screens in `spec/05-ui-prototype/`: prototype colors/cards/headers, five tabs Dashboard, Food & Water, Activities, Social, Account; developer dashboard keeps its own screen in the same style.**
A-33 | (stage 2) How to keep a no-Docker option and fast tests after the switch to MySQL; what happens to stage-1 PostgreSQL data | The `h2` profile and the test profile use H2 in MySQL mode with the same Flyway SQL. The V1 migration was rewritten in MySQL syntax (foreign keys as table constraints, `DATETIME(6)` timestamps) because a new database product starts empty; stage-1 PostgreSQL/H2 data is not migrated (it was test data only). | TRC README; D1 §5.3.2 "Encrypted Database"
A-34 | (stage 2) How the team's WATER_LOG table and LogWater unit fit the app's schema: column names, user id type, and what "fullName" is (team USERS has firstName/lastName; the class diagram User has only displayName) | Table `water_log(id, user_id BIGINT -> users.id, amount FLOAT(24) liters, logged_at DEFAULT now)`: the team's columns in this schema's snake_case and with the users key type (the team's `userId VARCHAR(64)` cannot reference an INT/BIGINT key). # Assumptions

Every gap that had to be filled because `spec/` (Project Proposal = "Prop", Deliverable 1 = "D1", Deliverable 2 draft = "D2",
team repo code = "TRC", team decisions = "TD-n") is silent or ambiguous. Code comments reference these IDs.
Rows answered by a later input are kept and marked **SUPERSEDED by ...** (stage 2).

A-n | what was missing | choice made | related spec section
---|---|---|---
A-1 | How the "Server" box (API gateway, auth gateway, 4 services, encrypted DB) is deployed; load balancing / telemetry details | One Spring Boot process with one package per box: `gateway` (API gateway + module routing), `security` (auth gateway), `controllers`+`services` (Social / Activity / Nutrition / Admin), PostgreSQL. Load balancing is not built for a laptop demo; telemetry = health checks + uptime records (FR-1). | D1 §5.3.1, §5.3.2, §5.3.3
A-2 | Which database product; Docker Engine not running on the build machine | PostgreSQL 16 (docker-compose) is the default. An `h2` Spring profile (embedded file DB, PostgreSQL mode) lets the app run and be tested without Docker. The same Flyway schema is used for both. | D1 §5.3.2 "Encrypted Database"; Prop §9 "Database for the app" **SUPERSEDED by `spec/04-team-repo-code/README.md` ("MySQL for database operations") and `db/docker-compose.yml` (`mysql:8.4`): database is now MySQL 8.4; see A-33.**
A-3 | How accounts are created (every use case includes "Log In" but there is no sign-up use case) | Students self-register (username, password, email, display name) and get a TOTP secret to add to an authenticator app. Developer accounts are created by seed/config only. | D1 Fig 4.3 "Log In (Password + TOTP)"; NFR Security **SUPERSEDED (TOTP setup part) by `spec/03-team-decisions/TD-1.md` (1), (2): after sign-up the app shows "Add to authenticator app" and "Copy setup key", and a QR code only on larger screens; self-registration itself is unchanged. See A-39.**
A-4 | Credential rules | Username 3–30 chars `[A-Za-z0-9_.]`, unique (case-insensitive); password ≥ 8 chars; email must look like an address. | NFR Security
A-5 | What "all user data will be encrypted" means concretely | Passwords: BCrypt hash. Email and TOTP secret: AES-256-GCM field encryption (key from `COMETFIT_DATA_KEY`). Other tables (meals, steps, …) rely on database/disk-level encryption in a real deployment, because the app must sum and query them. TLS is expected from the deployment's reverse proxy; the local demo uses plain HTTP. | NFR Security, NFR Legislative-Security; D1 §5.3.2 "Encrypted Database"
A-6 | Login flow detail and session lifetime | One login call carries username + password + 6-digit TOTP code; a Session (random 256-bit token, Bearer header) is created only if both factors pass, and lasts 12 h. `AuthService.authenticate` therefore takes the TOTP code as a third argument. TOTP = RFC 6238, SHA-1, 30 s, ±1 step. | D1 §5.2 AuthService, Session; NFR Security **SUPERSEDED (code on every sign-in) by `spec/03-team-decisions/TD-1.md` (3): "Remember this device for 30 days"; a remembered device signs in with username + password only. Session lifetime and TOTP parameters unchanged. See A-39.**
A-7 | Default goals for a new student | 2000 kcal, 2000 ml water, 10 000 steps, 500 ml bottle. Students can change them. | D1 §5.2 Student (calorieGoal, waterGoalMl, stepGoal)
A-8 | Where the water-bottle size lives (Prop: "volume of the user's water bottle … number of refills"; SD-1 "log water (bottle size / refill)"; class diagram has no field) | Added `bottleSizeMl` to Student (set in Profile → Goals). The app logs a refill as `saveWaterEntry(bottleSizeMl)`, plus half bottle or a custom amount. | Prop §4; D1 SD-1
A-9 | What "daily" means (time zone of the day boundary) | Configurable `COMETFIT_ZONE`, default America/Chicago (D1 cites the Texas Data Privacy and Security Act, so the users are in Texas). | D1 UC-1 "View Daily Summary & Goals"
A-10 | Thresholds for an "unsafe goal" | Warn when calorie goal < 1200 or > 4000 kcal, water goal < 1000 or > 4000 ml, step goal > 30 000 (Prop risk "User over-exertion → Warnings of the app"). The goal is still saved; the app only warns (NFR says "allow a warning"). | D1 NFR Safety; Prop §8
A-11 | Which "portions of the app" can be shut down | Three modules, each mapped to an API prefix: NUTRITION (`/api/nutrition`), ACTIVITY (`/api/activity`), SOCIAL (`/api/social`). Login, profile and admin cannot be disabled. A disabled module answers 503 `MODULE_DISABLED`, and the client shows a maintenance notice on those tabs. | FR-5; D1 UC-4, SD-4 ("disable module (e.g. Friends)")
A-12 | How external systems (UREC card reader, monitoring service) authenticate | Shared secret in header `X-Integration-Key` (`COMETFIT_INTEGRATION_KEY`). Card readers must also be registered in `urec_card_readers`; seed reader `UREC-FRONT-1` at "UREC front desk". | D1 §5.3.2 External Systems; SD-2, SD-4; NFR Security
A-13 | Names and contents of the "backend permissions list" | Students implicitly hold `nutrition.use`, `activity.use`, `social.use`, `profile.use`. Developers hold an explicit list; the seeded developer has `admin.uptime.view`, `admin.modules.manage`, `profile.use`. Developers do not get student features. | D1 NFR Security; §5.2 Developer.permissions; UC-4 "Authorize Admin (Permissions + TOTP)"
A-14 | Data for a recorded demo | When `COMETFIT_SEED_DEMO=true` (default), seed developer `dev` and students `alice` and `bob`, password `CometFit123!`, with fixed, published TOTP secrets. Demo only; turn it off anywhere real. | PROMPT (demoable in a video)
A-15 | Behaviour of the "AI Food Recognition Service" | Stub: picks 1–2 entries from a fixed placeholder table, deterministically from the image's SHA-256. The estimate is shown for review and is saved only after the student confirms or edits it. The photo itself is not stored. | D1 UC-1 "Log Meal by Photo"; SD-1; Prop §2
A-16 | UTD Dining menu content and locations | Stub feed with two locations, "Dining Hall" and "Campus Store" (from FR-8's rationale "campus stores and dining hall"), and 5 placeholder items each. Each `getMenu` call refreshes items from the feed into `dining_items` (keyed by the feed's item id), so meal entries can reference them. | FR-8; D1 UC-1 "Maintain Dining Menu & Macros"; §5.2 DiningItem
A-17 | Meaning of `steps` in a pushed ActivityRecord | Steps counted since the previous sync (an increment). Daily steps = sum of the day's records. Limits per push: steps 0–100 000, heart rate 20–250 bpm. | D1 SD-2 "pushSteps(steps, heartRate, timestamp)"; §5.2 ActivityRecord
A-18 | Default data-sharing consent | All four `share*` flags default to false; nothing is visible to friends until the student turns it on. | D1 NFR Legislative-Privacy; §5.2 ConsentSettings **SUPERSEDED for the seeded demo accounts only by `spec/03-team-decisions/TD-2.md`: alice and bob start with all four sharing flags on. Real new accounts keep everything off (this row still applies to them). See A-40.**
A-19 | When water intake is "too low" (FR-6 verification) | Any time today's total is below the student's water goal, the daily summary includes a "water intake is low" message. Reaching the goal shows a "goal reached" message instead. | FR-6 RTM verification method (D1 §4.4)
A-20 | Point values and limits | UREC visit: 10 points, awarded only for the first visit of each day (later swipes are still recorded). Reaching the daily step goal: 5 points, once per day. Points are never deducted. | Prop §3 "point based system"; D1 UC-2 "Earn Points", SD-2 `awardPoints(studentId, VISIT)`
A-21 | What the leaderboard ranks and who appears on it | Rank = point balance (ties share a rank), among the student and their friends. Points come only from visits and steps, so a friend appears (and their points show in their stats) only if they share visits or steps. | D1 UC-3 "View Leaderboard"; NFR Legislative-Privacy; Prop §7 leaderboard
A-22 | What `isPublic` controls | Non-friends viewing a private profile see only the username, not the display name or member-since date. Search by username always works, so friend requests are still possible. | D1 §5.2 User.isPublic; FR-3; Prop §4 "user-entered public information"
A-23 | How the friend is "notified of request" (Prop excludes push notifications) | In-app only: the request appears in the receiver's *Friend requests* list. | D1 SD-3 "notify of request"; Prop §4 Out of Scope
A-24 | Delivery channel for downtime alerts and when to send one | Stub `LoggingAlertNotifier`: logs a WARN line and keeps the last 50 alerts for the admin dashboard. An alert fires when a service goes down (first down check) and again when it recovers, not on every check. | D1 UC-4 "Raise Downtime Alert"; SD-4 alt [service down]
A-25 | Which "servers" are monitored, how often, how long records are kept | 7 components named after the §5.3.2 boxes (api-gateway, auth-gateway, nutrition-service, activity-service, social-service, admin-service, database), each with a real probe. Checks run every 30 s (configurable); uptime % is the share of successful checks over the chosen window (default 24 h). Records are kept 30 days. | FR-1; D1 SD-4 loop [every interval]; §5.2 MonitoringService.checkIntervalSec
A-26 | Client technology, given "mobile app only, no web application" (Prop §4, §7) vs. the requirement that the demo runs in a browser | Cross-platform Expo / React Native app (NFR Development: "native or cross-platform mobile app"). The same app is run through react-native-web for the laptop demo; this is a way to run the mobile client, not a separate web product. The phone-sized layout is kept. | Prop §4 Out of Scope; D1 NFR Operational, NFR Development; PROMPT
A-27 | What the UREC card carries to identify the student | The card reader sends the student's CometFit user id as `studentId` (the class diagram has no separate card-number field). | D1 SD-2 `recordVisit(studentId, time)`; §5.2 UrecCardReader.sendSwipe(studentId)
A-28 | Smart-device link rules | A health-data permission must be granted before linking (UC-2 «include» Grant Health Permissions). A device can be LINKED to only one student at a time. Optional automatic sync runs every 60 s while the Activity screen is open. | D1 UC-2, SD-2; NFR Interoperability
A-29 | Editing or deleting logged meals, water or visits | Not provided; the spec only describes logging and viewing. | D1 UC-1, UC-2
A-30 | Range of friend statistics | A friend's stats show today's calories, water and steps (with goals), UREC visits in the last 7 days, point balance, and leaderboard rank, each only if consented. | D1 UC-3 "View Friend's Statistics"; SD-3
A-31 | Brute-force protection and rate limiting | Not implemented (out of scope for the course prototype). The login error message is the same for every failure, so usernames can't be probed. | D1 NFR Security

A-33 | (stage 2) How to keep a no-Docker option and fast tests after the switch to MySQL; what happens to stage-1 PostgreSQL data | The `h2` profile and the test profile use H2 in MySQL mode with the same Flyway SQL. A-34 | (stage 2) How the team's WATER_LOG table and LogWater unit fit the app's schema: column names, user id type, and what "fullName" is (team USERS has firstName/lastName; the class diagram User has only displayName) | Table `water_log(id, user_id BIGINT -> users.id, amount FLOAT(24) liters, logged_at DEFAULT now)`: the team's columns in this schema's snake_case and with the users key type (the team's `userId VARCHAR(64)` cannot reference an INT/BIGINT key).
